quote: Oh my goodness. Yeah. 600 is quite expensive. But we can definitely help you get that cut down quite a bit.
stewart_read: The rep captures the bill and reacts with surprise, but the acknowledgment is generic reassurance ('we can help you get that cut down') rather than a flip that ties the $600 pain to urgency or to why the appointment matters. This is capture-and-move-on, the schema's named failure pattern.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep could be deliberately holding the flip for later in the call when booking the appointment, but no such callback ever occurs — the call ends without referencing the bill again.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to use the $600 figure explicitly when transitioning to next steps — e.g., tying the appointment to 'getting that $600 down' — instead of a one-line acknowledgment that gets buried in the verify flow.

stewart_read: A brand-new metal standing-seam roof on a brand-new home is a strong qualification signal — no re-roof risk, likely long tenure, ideal roof type for solar. The rep notes it ('Oh, okay... good to know') but never uses it as reassurance or momentum ('that's great news, means we don't have to worry about roof replacement at all').
coaching_implication: Point out to the rep that a new-build/new-roof answer is a chance to build confidence in the pitch ('one less thing to worry about') rather than just filing it as a data point.

quote: I'm not looking for that right now.
stewart_read: Customer signals she doesn't want to stop and pull up her bill mid-call. Rep repeats the same ask once more before pivoting, rather than immediately offering the text-later alternative the schema recommends for exactly this friction.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read is more supported here — the rep had the text-follow-up option available and used it, just one exchange later than optimal, not as a deliberate delay tactic.
coaching_implication: Coach faster recognition of a soft decline — pivot to the text/photo alternative on the first 'not right now' instead of asking a second time.

quote: Okay. I'll send that text right now, and then we will keep in touch.
stewart_read: The call ends with no day/time offered, no one-hour block mentioned, no 'is that fair' handshake, and no recap. 'We will keep in touch' is a passive close with no owned next step.
coaching_implication: This is the priority fix: after sending the bill-request text, the rep should still lock a specific callback day/time on the call itself rather than leaving the next contact undefined.

quote: And then I kinda wanna ask what what got you interested in solar?
stewart_read: The rep asks the interest question directly per script, and the customer gives a clear, usable answer ('To lower energy cost'). This is a correctly-run verify item.
coaching_implication: No coaching needed on the ask itself — the gap is that the answer ('lower energy cost') is never tied back into the bill discussion or the close, a missed reinforcement rather than a missed ask.

quote: K. And then I have you down as the property owner. Is there anybody else on the title of the home with you?
stewart_read: Rep runs the co-owner check correctly and gets a clean 'No' — no co-decider protocol is needed here, so this is a clean pass with nothing further required.
coaching_implication: None — flagged only to confirm this verify item was completed properly.
